checks: Full-dimensionality makes any nonempty strict residual have positive volume. If both endpoint residuals are nonempty, compact truncation and actual midpoint inclusion imply the opposite of a strict failure. With both empty there is no failure.
The single positive residual root exceeds 2(1−p)^{1/d} times the middle volume root. For p=0, full-fiber Brunn–Minkowski rules out failure.

At p≤γ_d, the surviving root normalized by the middle root exceeds √2>5/4. The other root is at most 2−b. Monotonicity of b^d−(2−b)^d and its value at 5/4, at least one, give the locally heavy conclusion. Since γ_d<1/2 the uniform growth factor exceeds 2^{d−1}.

The explicit scaled homothets are exact integer fibers at −1,0,1 and approach the strict mass factor from above for every fixed p in (0,1). The common affine cap can be given the stipulated full and empty endpoint statuses with finite tilt.

Growth excludes directed cycles, and outdegree at most one implies an undirected cycle would have one outgoing edge at every cycle vertex and so be directed. Multiplying the strict mass growth along the path gives the claimed bound.
